reasoning: The package consists of standard NVIDIA driver packaging artifacts (PKGBUILD, modprobe configs, systemd overrides, udev rules, and kernel patches). The 'inconclusive' verdict from the first model was solely due to a transient LLM API error (HTTP 400) on a benign modprobe config file, not a security finding. The second model successfully reviewed all files and found no malicious code or supply-chain injection. The third report is advisory-only and does not count toward the verdict.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was an artifact of a transient API failure (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in the qwen model when processing nvidia-580xx-utils.conf, which forced an inconclusive package verdict. The deepseek model processed the same file without issue and correctly identified it as a standard modprobe configuration.
coverage_issues: The audit tool's binary detection heuristic incorrectly flagged 0001-Enable-atomic-kernel-modesetting-by-default.patch as a binary file, causing all models to skip it. Patches are text files and must be audited for injected malicious code.
learnings: Improve the binary file detection logic in the file materialization/selection phase to correctly identify text-based patch files (.patch) and prevent them from being skipped.
Add retry logic or graceful degradation for transient LLM API errors (like HTTP 400/500) so that a single file's API failure does not cascade into an inconclusive package verdict.
